provenance: Opus 5.5 subscription CLI draft with host review/repairs, source restrictions and execution verification.

draft_notes.explanation: The mechanism is a 4-connected flood fill of the cells that have the original colour 0, now palette[0]. Each component is checked for whether it touches any of the four grid edges. Edge-touching components become palette[2]. Fully enclosed components become palette[5]. All other cells (palette[1] and palette[3] walls) stay unchanged. The edge set and 4-neighbourhood map onto themselves under every D4 transform, so the visible-coordinate program is the same for every d4. Only the colour constants are specialised through the palette. The program works on any rectangular grid size, and a grid that is one cell wide or tall counts as all-border.
draft_notes.limitations: Colour roles come from the palette, not inferred from the demonstrations. The constructor itself only makes 10x10 grids from colours {0,1,3} and rejects scenes where the output has fewer than 4 colours. No constructor defects or tie-breaks were found: the generator's stack-based flood fill gives the same result as component-wise border-touch classification. The fixtures agree with this uniform rule. Not executed or tested by me.
